newsitem.title: USA: Toyota unveils electric RAV4-EV sport/utility.
newsitem.headline: Toyota unveils electric RAV4-EV sport/utility.

text.p: Toyota Thursday unveiled its RAV4-EV electric vehicle, the latest entry in the popular sport/utility class.

It will go on sale in mid-October, with a suggested retail price of $42,000. The lease price will be $499 per month for 36 months with no mileage restrictions, according to Toyota Motor Sales, USA Inc. the U.S. unit of Japanese automaker Toyota Motor Corp.

The RAV4-EV is identical in size and shape to Toyota's four-door RAV sport/utility vehicle. But the RAV4-EV uses nickel-metal hydride batteries for power, reaching speeds up to 79 miles per hour with a city/highway range of 120 miles. The batteries charge can be charged from a regular household electrical outlet and require no additional equipment.

"We began our electric vehicle programme with extensive in-house testing, moved to real-world driving with test-fleet partners, and are now ready to make production vehicles available to fleet buyers," said Dave Illingworth, general manager of the Toyota U.S. division. "We fully believe that this is the finest full-electric vehicle produced today."
California mandates that 10 percent of all vechicles sold in the state by any manufacturer must be non-polluting, zero-emission vechicles by 2003.
General Motors Corp. recently launched its electric vehicle, called the EV-1.
Toyota is targeting fleet sales to commercial users and businesses with the RAV4-EV. It expects initial sales to concentrate in California and the northeastern United States.
Incentives and purchase assistance programmes worth up to $9,000 are available through local and federal agencies.
